target_customer: Hardware companies and OEMs that manufacture in China, and the factories that build for them
problem: Companies that outsource manufacturing to China struggle to verify that test protocols are followed, which causes defects, liability and warranty fraud. Assembly puts cameras and monitoring software on the line.
business_model: Per unit fee charged to the OEM with revenue sharing to the factory when units meet quality standards (YC page); GetScale used a subscription from $110 per station per month in 2015
product_category: Factory quality monitoring and compliance (formerly GetScale)

founders.name: Jonathan Friedman
education: Ph.D. in electrical engineering (per YC page)
previous_startups: CircuitHub (YC alumnus, electronics manufacturing service, cofounded about 2012, outcome not researched)
founders.background_notes: YC page: background in biomedical and industrial systems engineering, 2x YC founder. TechCrunch July 2015: he stayed in factory dorms in China before launching.

founders.name: Colton Pierson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch July 2015 says Friedman and Pierson started GetScale in January 2014 after working together at CircuitHub. The YC page lists only Friedman.

competitors.name: Automated optical inspection equipment (Keysight, Agilent)
competitors.traction_then: Established category; TechCrunch says machines often cost more than $250,000 each

competitors.name: Sending executives or engineers to visit factories
competitors.what: In person factory audits by the customer
competitors.traction_then: The common alternative GetScale clients cited as costly

technical_complexity.rationale: Camera stations, barcode capture, remote monitoring software and integration into Chinese factory floors; hardware logistics across Shenzhen and Shanghai added difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Factory relationships and compliance records could lock in customers, but camera and software monitoring was replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows the incumbents copying it. Later computer vision factory monitoring startups appear in search results, which are not dated near the batch.

market_need_then: TechCrunch July 2015: about 20 clients including iCracked, Neurolabware and Napwell, 250,000 units inspected in six months, offices in Redwood City, Shenzhen and Shanghai.

branding.name_origin: YC page and search result say the company started in 2014 as GetScale and became Assembly; no reason for the new name was found.
branding.domain_note: Uses asm.co per the YC directory

brand_strength.rationale: Assembly is an extremely generic name shared with many unrelated companies (a Quirky backed software platform, a virtual events startup, a client portal), and search for this company returned mostly those others.

outcome_analysis: GetScale, renamed Assembly, sold factory monitoring to hardware companies in China and had early traction in 2015, but no later funding, exit or status change could be found. The YC directory shows it active with about 12 people. The outcome is unclear, and the generic name makes the company hard to trace in later press.
notes: asm.co could not be fetched: the host did not resolve in this session's network, so the site state is unknown rather than known dead. The YC page says Friedman founded it in 2014 and a search result lists South San Francisco while the YC list says Los Angeles. No funding found; two outcome searches returned unrelated companies named Assembly (Quirky Assembly with USV $2.9M in 2014 and a client portal formerly Copilot), which are not this company. Brand effect marked hurt only on the basis of name genericness and search confusion, a weak inference, but unclear would hide the confusion.
